item.title: Hillingdon Council secures conviction against TfL cab driver over PSPO breach near Heathrow
item.description: Image Credit: Hillingdon Council Hillingdon Council has successfully prosecuted a Transport for London (TfL) licensed cab driver for breaching a Public Spaces Protection Order and failing to pay a Fixed Penalty Notice, reinforcing its enforcement stance around Heathrow-adjacent residential areas. item.title: Regulator explores easing or potentially removing UK contactless payment limits to support growth
item.description: The UK’s Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) is assessing whether removing or raising the current contactless payment limit could benefit consumers, merchants and wider economic growth, as part of a broader push to make financial regulation less prescriptive. In an engagement paper, the regulator said greater flexibility on contactless limits could deliver smoother transactions for households and businesses, while giving payment firms more control over how limits are set and managed. item.title: Manchester taxi grants raise questions over potential pressure on London’s second-hand black cab market
item.description: Greater Manchester’s £12,560 Hackney Support Fund grant is already being welcomed by drivers locally, but attention is now turning south to what the scheme could mean for London’s tightly balanced second-hand black cab market. The concern being voiced quietly across the trade is simple. Manchester licensed drivers, armed with a sizeable grant and additional manufacturer support, may find themselves in a stronger purchasing position than London drivers when competing for used LEVC TX vehicles...

item.title: LICENSING INQUIRY: Councils accuse Wolverhampton of fuelling cross border private hire licensing by allowing out-of-area MOT and onboarding
item.description: Salford City Council have told MPs that Wolverhampton City Council’s approach to taxi and private hire licensing has “opened up the floodgates” to drivers and vehicles operating hundreds of miles away from the city. In further written evidence to Parliament , the councils argue that Wolverhampton’s systems and practices have materially accelerated national out-of-area licensing, creating enforcement and safety challenges elsewhere. item.title: AIRPORT FIXED PRICE FARES: As ever in the taxi trade, one region’s common sense is another’s chaos
item.description: There’s no shortage of opinion when it comes to airport fares, and TaxiPoint’s latest industry question about whether drivers would support fixed price airport taxi fares has stirred up quite a mix of responses. From Glasgow to the Wirral, cabbies had plenty to say, and the split in opinions shows just how complex this issue is across different licensing areas. For some, fixed airport fares are nothing new. item.title: Taxi drivers warned over serial fare dodger operating in Mayfair as police build up case
item.description: London taxi drivers are being urged to stay alert after reports emerged of a suspected serial fare dodger targeting cabs in the Mayfair area, according to the Licensed Taxi Drivers’ Association (LTDA) . item.title: Avon and Somerset Police issues 40 tickets during Bristol taxi rank enforcement operation
item.description: Image credit: PC Quinton / Avon and Somerset Police Avon and Somerset Police issued around 40 penalty notices during a taxi and private hire vehicle enforcement operation in Bristol aimed at keeping taxi ranks and waiting areas clear for licensed drivers. item.title: Lincolnshire taxi driver loses licence appeal after videos show cabbie speeding and watching videos on mobile
item.description: A Scunthorpe taxi driver has failed in his attempt to overturn the immediate revocation of his licence after magistrates ruled he was not fit and proper to carry passengers. At a hearing on 5 December 2025 , Grimsby Magistrates’ Court upheld the decision by North Lincolnshire Council to revoke the licence of Mr Shah Abu Sufian Md Sheruzzaman Siddiquee with immediate effect. item.title: Lyft plan to launch ‘dozens’ of autonomous vehicles on Freenow platform in London next year as part of testing
item.description: Image credit: Lyft / Baidu Lyft has confirmed plans to begin testing autonomous vehicles in London next year through the Freenow platform, marking the first deployment of Baidu’s Apollo Go robotaxi technology in the UK and the wider region. item.title: Police appeal after taxi collision leaves man seriously injured in Colchester
item.description: Essex Police have issued an appeal for information after a silver Nissan taxi was involved in a serious collision with a pedestrian in Colchester, leaving a man with significant injuries. The incident occurred on Highwoods Approach at around 3.50pm on Friday 12 December. Police said the man was taken to hospital, where he remains being treated for serious injuries.
